description: PRD-108: Memory Field Prototype — Full research + design PRD. Study shared vector spaces, resonance mechanics, decay algorithms. Design the experiment that tests whether shared semantic fields outperform message passing. This is the Phase 3 gate — if the prototype doesn't prove value, Phase 3 is reassessed.

userStories.title: Research shared vector space implementations
userStories.description: As a researcher, I need to study production vector stores and shared memory patterns so that our prototype uses the right foundation
acceptanceCriteria: Study FAISS — index types (IVF, HNSW), shared memory mode, multi-process access, Python bindings
Study Qdrant — collections, shared access, filtering, payload indexing, gRPC API
Study Redis vector search (RediSearch) — vector similarity, hybrid queries, pub/sub integration
Study Pinecone — namespaces, metadata filtering, serverless vs pod-based
Study existing S3 Vectors setup in Automatos — what's already configured
Study temporal decay in information retrieval — TF-IDF time decay, exponential forgetting curves
Comparison table: system, shared access model, latency, scale, cost, decay support
Write to PRD section: '## 2. Prior Art: Shared Vector Spaces'
Recommend vector store for prototype with rationale
userStories.notes: S3 Vectors is already configured (automatos-vector-index). Redis is already running for sessions/pub-sub. FAISS is used by Agent Zero. Consider what's ALREADY AVAILABLE before adding new infrastructure. The prototype should work with existing infra if possible.

userStories.title: Research resonance and decay mechanisms
userStories.description: As a researcher, I need to study how information amplification and decay work in theory and practice
acceptanceCriteria: Read Context Engineering repo: 08_neural_fields_foundations.md — neural field theory
Read Context Engineering repo: 09_persistence_and_resonance.md — resonance mechanics
Read Context Engineering repo: 11_emergence_and_attractor_dynamics.md — convergence
Study Hebbian learning: 'neurons that fire together wire together' — how it maps to semantic reinforcement
Study attention mechanisms in transformers — self-attention as a resonance computation
Study TF-IDF time decay variants — how relevance diminishes over time in IR systems
Define resonance formula with concrete parameters: R(A, B) = cos(θ) × |A| × |B| × S(A, B) from PRD-100
Define decay formula with concrete parameters: S(t) = S₀ × e^(-λt) from PRD-100
Write to PRD section: '## 3. Resonance & Decay: Theory to Implementation'
Include worked numerical examples showing resonance amplification and decay
userStories.notes: The Context Engineering repo is at /Users/gkavanagh/Development/Automatos-AI-Platform/Context-Engineering/00_foundations/. This is where theory meets implementation — the formulas from PRD-100 need concrete parameter values. What's λ? How do we measure S(A, B)? These must be answerable.

userStories.title: Design the prototype architecture
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need the prototype scoped as a minimal, testable experiment
acceptanceCriteria: Define prototype scope: 2-3 agents, 1 shared field, 1 mission, controlled test
Define field operations: inject(embedding, metadata), query(embedding, k, min_relevance), decay_tick()
Define field data structure: vector + metadata (source_agent, timestamp, reinforcement_count, current_strength)
Define resonance computation: when agent B injects, check similarity with existing entries, amplify aligned entries
Define decay computation: periodic sweep that reduces strength, removes entries below threshold
Write to PRD section: '## 4. Prototype Architecture'
Include system diagram showing agents ↔ field ↔ vector store
Include Python pseudocode for core field operations (<100 lines)
Explicitly scope: what the prototype does NOT include (K8s, multiple fields, attractor detection)
userStories.notes: The prototype must be simple enough to build in a few days. Think: a Python class (MemoryField) backed by FAISS or Redis vectors, with inject/query/decay methods. Agents call inject() after producing output, call query() before starting work. That's it.

userStories.title: Design the experiment
userStories.description: As a researcher, I need a rigorous experiment design so that the prototype test produces meaningful results
acceptanceCriteria: Define experiment hypothesis: 'Shared semantic field produces higher quality multi-agent outputs than message passing for tasks requiring cross-agent context'
Define control condition: same mission, same agents, message-passing coordination (Phase 2 adapter from PRD-107)
Define treatment condition: same mission, same agents, shared field coordination (prototype field)
Define test mission: a multi-step task where cross-agent context matters (e.g., 'research topic X, then write report incorporating research')
Define evaluation metrics: output quality (human eval + LLM judge), context utilization (how much cross-agent context appears in outputs), token efficiency (total tokens used), latency
Define sample size: how many mission runs needed for meaningful comparison
Write to PRD section: '## 5. Experiment Design'
Include evaluation rubric for human assessors
Address: confirmation bias mitigation — blind evaluation, multiple evaluators
userStories.notes: PRD-100 Risk #6: 'Context Engineering theory doesn't translate to code.' This experiment is the gate. Be honest about what constitutes a pass and a fail. If shared field is only marginally better or adds too much complexity, that's a valid finding.

userStories.title: Design pass/fail criteria for Phase 3 gate
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need clear criteria for whether the prototype justifies continuing to Phase 3
acceptanceCriteria: Define PASS criteria (proceed to Phase 3): measurable improvement in output quality, reasonable latency (<200ms field operations), manageable complexity
Define FAIL criteria (reassess Phase 3): no quality improvement, unacceptable latency, resonance/decay add noise not signal
Define PARTIAL criteria (modify Phase 3 scope): some improvements in specific scenarios, not universal
Define minimum bar: field must outperform message-passing on at least 2 of 4 metrics
Write to PRD section: '## 6. Phase 3 Gate Criteria'
Address: what 'reassess Phase 3' means practically — simplified version, delayed, or abandoned
Address PRD-100 Risk #8: 'Neural field resonance is just RAG with extra steps'
userStories.notes: Be intellectually honest here. PRD-100 Risk #10 says 'Phase 2 already delivers enough value, Phase 3 never starts' and calls this 'actually fine.' The gate criteria should reflect that — Phase 3 must earn its complexity budget.

userStories.title: Design integration with PRD-107 context interface
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need the prototype to implement the ContextPort from PRD-107 so that it's a real adapter swap
acceptanceCriteria: Show how MemoryField maps to ContextPort methods from PRD-107
inject_context → MemoryField.inject() with embedding generation
query_context → MemoryField.query() with resonance scoring
build_system_prompt → standard ContextService.render() + field-augmented context
Define embedding model for field operations — use existing qwen3-embedding-8b (2048 dims) from config
Write to PRD section: '## 7. Context Interface Integration'
Verify prototype can be tested via adapter swap without coordinator changes
userStories.notes: This is where PRD-107 and PRD-108 meet. The experiment (US-004) should work by swapping adapters: run mission with MessagePassingContextAdapter, then run same mission with NeuralFieldContextAdapter. Same coordinator, same agents, different context layer.
